newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PSG WIN AT HOME FOR FIRST TIME SINCE NOVEMBER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PSG WIN AT HOME FOR FIRST TIME SINCE NOVEMBER.

text.p: Paris St Germain scored twice in the last three minutes on Sunday as they came from behind to beat Lyon 3-1 to record their first win in eight home matches since November.
Captain Rai scored twice, heading the crucial equaliser two minutes into the second half from a corner by fellow Brazilian Leonardo. Striker Cedric Bardon had put Lyon ahead in the 10th minute.
France striker Patrice Loko gave PSG the lead in the 87th minute and Rai added the third a minute later.
Earlier centre-back Bruno N'Gotty headed against the Lyon bar and goalkeeper Bernard Lama made a crucial save with his foot from striker Alain Caveglia, the visitors' top scorer this season.
PSG had not won at the Parc des Princes in six league games and two European matches since beating Lille 3-1 on November 13.
They sunk into deep crisis after a home loss to relegation candidates Nancy in December and a 6-1 drubbing by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup in January.
The European Cup Winners' Cup holders were also held 0-0 at home by AEK Athens in the first leg of their quarter-final tie on Thursday, failing to translate territorial dominance into goals.
Sunday's victory put PSG just three points behind leaders Monaco whose home match with defending champions Auxerre kicked off shortly after the match in Paris ended.
On Saturday, Nantes extended their unbeaten league run to 21 games when they beat third-placed Bastia 3-0 at home. The win enhanced six-placed Nantes' hopes of a berth in Europe next season.
